finding: About a quarter of REGDOCS documents are not digital documents.
evidence: 23.2% of 5,000 random documents (95% CI 22.1-24.4%) mostly scans, stub layers, broken layers or text as graphics; pages: 65% digital, 11% digital+images, 15% image only, 5% scanner OCR, 2% stub.

finding: Non-digital filing is falling.
evidence: 28-47% of documents in most years before 2012; 6-10% in 2021-2026 (2024's 32% is one filer, F009).

finding: The documents that are scans are the signed ones; affidavits most of all.
evidence: Mostly not digital: affidavits 79% (64-89%), letters 23% (21-26%), letters of comment 20%; orders 3%, receipts 0%.

finding: Print-sign-scan is fading for letters but not for affidavits.
evidence: Signed documents mostly scanned: 2012-16 34% (20-51%), 2017-21 11%, 2022-26 11%; affidavits 6 of 6 scanned.

finding: What made the PDF predicts whether it is digital far better than its content does.
evidence: Mostly not digital by tool kind: reporting 0%, office 1%, print drivers 4%, PostScript 7%, PDF libraries 11%, PDF editors 21%, no producer recorded 75%, scanners 98%.

finding: Scanner OCR layers are mostly good, but a quarter of pages are not, for some scanners.
evidence: Median agreement with our OCR 76-96% by producer; 19-28% of pages under 60% for Xerox, EPSON, Acrobat, Paper Capture; OmniPage 5%, Canon 6%.

finding: Canon, Xerox and EPSON scanner OCR layers match a third to a half of the page.
evidence: Samples: medians Canon 36%, Xerox 33%, EPSON 51%.
why_wrong: set by a few poor documents in a sample of a few hundred

finding: A stamp or markup on a scan makes it look searchable when it is not (stub layer).
evidence: 2% of pages; RICOH 17%, Canon 14%, Adobe Acrobat 9% of pages; a stub holds ~20 of a page's hundreds of words.

finding: 92% of RICOH pages and 59% of Bluebeam pages are stub layers.
evidence: Samples.
why_wrong: each rate set by one filing

finding: Text drawn as vector outlines cannot be searched or copied; rare but total where it happens.
evidence: 0.4% of pages; Microsoft Print to PDF exhibit lists (3,129 paths, 0 characters a page); CAD drawings via PostScript/pdfFactory (up to 205,000 paths a page).

finding: 35% of Microsoft Print to PDF pages are text drawn as graphics.
evidence: Samples.

finding: Some digital documents are turned into pictures by the filer's publishing system - no paper involved.
evidence: 81 of 5,000 random documents: Trans Mountain IR responses (2024, iText), born-digital pages as 300 dpi images with no text (4461679).

finding: About one image-only page in four is a digital page rasterized, not scanned paper.
evidence: 40 random image-only pages judged by eye: 29 paper, 11 rasterized digital (28%, ~16-43%). Pixel statistics cannot tell them apart.

finding: A redaction drawn over text leaves the text readable.
evidence: 4710294: 13,159 words on 36 pages under black boxes still in the text layer; anyone copying the page reads them.

finding: Covered redactions are rare in a random survey.
evidence: No case in 5,000 documents (3 pages each). A first count of 7 were glyphs on dark boxes (checkboxes, bullets, map symbols).

finding: 7 of 5,000 documents have text under cover-up redactions.
evidence: Detector count.
why_wrong: each hit was one glyph on a dark box; a redaction hides words

finding: Some text layers do not decode to the characters shown; CAD most of all.
evidence: 0.5% of pages overall; Bentley MicroStation 19%, Ghostscript 3%. 2026-09 corpus: one filing 315 of 986 pages.

finding: Structure rarely travels with the document.
evidence: Tagged 47%; PDF/A 0.4%; bookmarks on documents over 20 pages 50%; live form fields 67 of 5,000; checkboxes printed flat in 39 sample documents.

finding: Oversize sheets are common enough to plan for.
evidence: 113 of 5,000 documents (2.3%) have sheets over 17.5 in; 2026-09 corpus: 13 pages up to 182 in could not be processed.

finding: Sideways scans, numbered paper and duplex blank backs are not worth requiring anything about.
evidence: 9 of 29 scans sideways, read fine by OCR; numbered paper reads cleanly; blank backs 0.3% of pages, recognised.

finding: Records before 2012 lacked facets because they were never enriched, not because REGDOCS lacks them.
evidence: 3,000 records: 2002-2011 none, 2012 on all; enriching one 2010 day returned full facets.

finding: REGDOCS serves some items listed as PDF as HTML pages, and some old documents are gone.
evidence: 41 items served as HTML (2023 filing receipts) excluded; 78 old documents answer 404.

finding: The text layer is the reliable reader when sound; structure readers only draw boxes over its words.
evidence: 320-420 sample documents: every evidence word named once in the DoclingDocument, item text and Markdown 100%.

finding: RapidOCR PP-OCRv6 medium reads best of the configurations tried.
evidence: 60 sound pages: v6 medium 92.5% of words at place, v6 small 89.9%, v5 mobile 88.1%, v5 server 77.0%, v4 mobile 75.3%.

finding: Vision models can vote on disputed lines only after a blank-page test; two write text on blanks.
evidence: 150 line crops: qwen3-vl 95.7% words, GLM-OCR 92.9% (no text on blanks); olmOCR-2 and DeepSeek-OCR wrote text on 6 of 6 blank crops.

finding: A vision model carries on past its answer; read only its first line and treat loops as abstentions.
evidence: GLM-OCR: 11 loops in 23 crops and text on every blank before; none after.

finding: Tables: TableFormer fast + accurate + ruling lines, chosen by fit, is the measured route.
evidence: 4,348 tables: 96.6% of words placed (accurate alone 95.2%, fast alone 91.3%). Values stacked in one cell do not count as placed.

finding: OCR at more rotations does not recover drawing labels worth its cost.
evidence: 60 digital drawings: 0 degrees 67.3% of labels, all four 71.4%, with 40-58 more junk words per 100; 300 dpi worse.

finding: Transcripts are known from their title or margin numbers and read as numbered lines, not tables.
Reading order: place items by their words; two-column pages remain the weakest.
evidence: Disagreement with the text layer's order, two-column median 0.127 to 0.100 after the fix.

finding: Samples of a few hundred documents find kinds of problem; rates need a random survey with intervals.
evidence: Three sample rates corrected by the 5,000-document survey (F006a, F007a, F008a).

finding: Check the canonical output as a consumer reads it, and look at the page before reporting.
evidence: The DoclingDocument check found picture text skipped by default iteration; the redaction detector's 7 hits were all false.

finding: A provenance field that can vanish silently needs its own check.
evidence: pyarrow from_pylist took columns from the first row; 2,084 of 2,606 votes per voter lost their OCR-model tag.

finding: Filers submit tables as CSV/Excel with a data dictionary, spatial data as GeoPackage with an EPSG code, drawings with DXF/DWG; CER stores Parquet/GeoParquet.
evidence: Proposed from F023/F024 and tool availability; shapefiles split into 3-7 files with 10-character fields; Parquet is rarely producible by filers.

finding: Document length is heavy-tailed, so a processing time limit must scale with pages (and with page size), not be fixed per document.
evidence: Survey of 5,000: median 3 pages, p99 171, max 7,280 (2498373); 4 documents of 500+ pages hold 13% of pages. Light pass: scanned documents 2.2-2.8 s/page (4672628, 691 pages, 31 min); 4724234 (171 pages, 125 A0 sheets) hit a fixed 1-hour limit, finished in 22 min on retry (7.7 s/page). Limit now max(1 h, 20 s x pages).

finding: A killed worker process still looks alive until reaped; join it before deciding whether to replace it, and treat any pipe error as a crash.
evidence: The corpus light pass stopped after 1,049 documents with ConnectionResetError after a timed-out worker was handed the next document. Fixed in 902024e.

finding: The documents that defeat converters are the same across tools and years: large files (35-45 MiB) with many pages needing OCR, not long documents as such.
evidence: cer-regdocs2 Docling run quarantined 10 IDs (8 files) after 1,200 s timeouts or segfaults, incl. 4647200 (986 p), 4672628 (691 p), 4664989 (450 p); Azure finished them by splitting into 300-page ranges. The 2026-10-13 light pass finished 9 of 10 (4672628 in 31 min) and timed out on 4647200 at a fixed hour; 315 of its 986 pages have an undecodable text layer (cer-regdocs4). The 285- and 297-page files that crashed docling took 22 s here (text layer only).

finding: Stop a document for making no progress, not for taking long: GPU contention between workers, not the document, makes scanned batches slow.
evidence: 4646037 (108 pages) took 635 s alone (364 s waiting on the GPU) but over 3,600 s in the pass beside other scanned documents from the same filing; 3 such timeouts in one hour cut the pass from ~17 to ~2.3 pages a second. Stall limit (no page finished in 900 s) added.

finding: Several GPU workers must hand back cached memory as they go: on WSL a full card spills to system memory and everything slows instead of failing.
evidence: 10 light-pass workers grew to 23.3 of 24.5 GB (PyTorch cache emptied only between documents); 4 ordinary documents stalled 15 minutes on a page, rate 6.7 pages/s. Emptying the cache after OCR above 1 GB per worker: peak 19.7 GB, 0 stalls, ~23 pages/s.

finding: A section tree comes from the filer's bookmarks when there are two or more, else from heading numbers that run in sequence; a heading number alone is as often a list, legend, note or OCR noise.
evidence: 77 random documents (random-100-a) in light mode: 4034412 118 sections / 7 levels from bookmarks (116 found on their pages); 777308 72 sections / 4 levels from numbering. False sections rejected: revision row '0 ...', slope legend '5 - 10-15%', drawing notes 1-15, OCR '2 B°' / '3 C64'. Evidence intact in 77 of 77.

finding: Keeping every reader's words makes assembly repeatable without the readers: a change to how pages are put together can reach the whole corpus without the GPU.
evidence: --reuse-ocr on 4657424 (149 pages, 64 OCR'd): 48 s vs 188 s, OCR model never loaded, all 41,735 words identical to the original conversion.

finding: Some pages hang the PDF library outright; skip the page (recorded as missing) and keep the rest of the document.
evidence: 4537539 p.130 (ArcGIS map, 69 nested form XObjects): MuPDF 1.28.2 neither extracts text nor renders it within minutes; other 169 pages under 1 s each. 11 documents stalled in one hour, 10 from one filing (4553641-4553652). Retry without the stuck page, at most 3 pages, stall limit 300 s.

finding: Keep a second renderer: a PDF library can crash drawing a page it reads fine, and another library draws it.
evidence: 4473998: MuPDF 1.28.2 heap corruption ('double free') rendering slides with a Display P3 JPEG under 30% transparency (p.41, 45, 56, 57, 59, 65); text extraction fine; pdfium renders all 65 pages in 1.8 s. Retry with pdfium for those pages: 65/65 pages kept.

finding: Running headers and footers are found by repetition across pages, not by layout models: the four-model vote labels only 40% of repeated band lines as furniture, and most of the rest are running heads.
evidence: 274 full-mode sample documents (>=4 pages): 13,322 lines in the top/bottom 12% repeating on >=3 pages and >=30% of pages, in 195 documents; layout called 40% page_header/page_footer; of 30 it called body, ~23 running heads, 2-3 repeated table header rows, ~4 unclear.

finding: Tables cross pages in about one document in six; a repeated header line identifies a continuation better than matching column counts, because each page's grid is read on its own.
evidence: 625 full-mode samples: 1,073 bottom-of-page/top-of-next table pairs in 103 documents; header line repeated (fuzzy) in 669 pairs / 49 documents; 123 pairs repeat the header with different column counts ([4,3], [13,12]).

finding: Pages are not units of meaning: most section headings start mid-page and about one page break in six splits a sentence, so text must be joined across breaks (keeping per-page provenance) and chunked by section, not page.
evidence: 430 full-mode documents: 12,274 of 17,487 headings not first on their page (70%); 1,173 of 5,903 page breaks end open and continue in lower case (20%), ~12 of 15 read are true sentence splits; 136 documents have one.

finding: Running heads repeat over a document's own span, not the whole file: test repetition against the span between first and last occurrence (and across the page, not inside a text cluster).
evidence: 4403940 (93 pages, several documents): an article's header on 26 pages (every other page from p.43) failed a 30%-of-file rule; per-cluster lines never repeated because clusters cut the header differently. With span-based repetition on page-wide lines: 20 rebuilt documents, evidence intact; 22 cross-page joins, ~19 true sentence splits.

finding: Stitching a table across pages works when the continuation is laid on the first page's columns rather than its own grid.
evidence: 103 full-mode documents with tables at page boundaries, rebuilt on the CPU from saved words/regions/grids: 186 stitches, evidence intact in all; 995751 one 33-row table over pp. 42-46 with columns aligned; 940189 items 6->7 across pp. 1-2.

finding: What REGDOCS will not list is stable, not transient: containers that report more members than they list do so the same way on every run, so they are recorded as known gaps rather than retried.
evidence: 2002-2011 enrichment: 47 unread items - 37 short containers (43 missing members), 5 unparsable result rows, 3 recorded gaps, 2 timeouts; a retry of 2009 and 2010 saw all 11 failures again.
